roles.name: Supply Chain Analyst
roles.blurb: Keeps critical spares and treatment chemicals available across the three businesses, checks spend is on contract at the contract price, and supports sourcing events with landed-cost analysis.

areas.name: Spend and contract compliance
areas.what: Knows what the group buys, from whom, and whether it is bought on contract at the contract price.
tasks: Report third-party spend against plan by business and category
Measure spend under contract and the leakage where a contract covers the item
Find invoices above the contract price
Track payment terms against the 45-day policy

areas.name: Sourcing and award support
areas.what: Gives category managers the analysis behind each sourcing event and award paper.
tasks: Build the volume baseline from dosing plans and run rates
Compare bids on landed cost: price, freight and index terms
Draft the award paper and schedule for the Procurement Committee

areas.name: Inventory and critical spares
areas.what: Keeps critical spares and chemicals above safety stock across 36 sites without carrying dead stock.
tasks: Watch critical positions against safety stock after every nightly load
Look across the group before an emergency buy

areas.name: Treatment chemical continuity
areas.what: Makes sure no plant runs short of a treatment chemical, whatever happens at a supplier.
tasks: Track days of cover per plant and chemical against the minimums
Size the exposure when a supplier declares force majeure
Arrange spot volume under exception FMX

areas.name: Outage material readiness
areas.what: Confirms that what a planned outage reserves is on site 14 days before it starts.
tasks: Check reservations against stock and promised dates
Arrange transfers and expedites for gaps
Report readiness to the outage manager

areas.name: Supplier performance
areas.what: Measures delivery, lead time and quality by supplier and follows through on corrective actions.
tasks: Publish quarterly scorecards: on time in full, lead time, price

areas.name: Savings program
areas.what: Keeps the FY26 savings register honest: what counts, what is secured, what is reported apart.
tasks: Record savings when they are in an order or a signed contract
Reconcile the tracker with Finance each month

areas.name: Reporting
areas.what: Turns the above into the monthly report and the committee pack.
tasks: Monthly procurement report after the close
Monthly shortage review with the buyers

questions.q: How many days of ferric chloride does each plant hold, against its minimum?

answer.text: Five water plants hold less than ten days of ferric chloride against the 14-day minimum: Fenmoor 6.2, Holloway Creek 7.4, Stanwick 8.1, Marston Reach 9.3, Quinton Lakes 9.6 days. 7 water plants are under 14. Two hazardous waste facilities hold 27 to 31 days against their 10-day minimum, but they use little ferric.

questions.q: What does the Corrigan force majeure expose, and what have the spot buys cost so far?

answer.figLabel: Spot premium so far · 360 tons since 12 October
answer.text: Since 12 October Corrigan has shipped 60% of ferric volume and Anika Sorensen has bought the rest on spot from Sabine Coast: 41 lines, 360 tons at $548 against $402, $52,604 above the contract. Five water plants are under ten days of cover. If the allocation lasted the whole of 2027 with Corrigan as primary, replacing 40% on spot would cost about $1.56M a year more.
